clue.text: Ferociously attack a guy initially in bar

indicators.note: in means the letters of a and the guy's first letter are placed inside the word for bar

parts.note: bar in the sense of except, as in 'all bar one', is save

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of the word guy

explanation.surface: A violent outburst in a pub, with some fellow set upon at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To maul or savage someone is to attack them with wild ferocity, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Squash and second form of exercise switched

indicators.note: switched means the two halves of the exercise's name swap places

parts.note: a press-up is a floor exercise pushing the body up with the arms

explanation.surface: A gym-goer swapping between squash and another workout routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squash' looks like the sport alongside exercise, but it is the verb meaning crush. 'Switched' turns PRESS-UP into UP-PRESS. A press-up is the British name for a push-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To squash a revolt or a feeling is to quash or stifle it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Ordinary article hidden under ceiling in house

indicators.note: the ceiling of the house word is its top letter, and the article sits just below it inside the word

parts.note: a villa is a large detached house
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something plain stowed away beneath the ceiling in a home.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the first letter is the top, so 'under ceiling' puts AN just beneath the V of VILLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is slang for plain or basic, with no extras, so it means ordinary.

clue.text: Piece of gold and lump of iron someone experimented on

parts.note: a guinea was an old British gold coin
a pig is an oblong cast block of crude iron from a smelter, hence pig iron

explanation.surface: A list of metal treasures turns out to describe a test subject.
explanation.walkthrough: A guinea was an old British gold coin worth twenty-one shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: A person used as the subject of a trial or test is commonly called by this rodent's name.

clue.text: Finishes off operation for pains

definitions.meaning: a surgeon closes an incision with sutures at the end of surgery
sharp aches in the side, as after running, are known by this name

explanation.surface: Someone completes a procedure on behalf of their aches.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutures close a wound after surgery, and a sudden side ache from exercise has the same name, so both senses fit one word.

clue.text: Fearful inaccuracies are misleading in part of political address

indicators.note: in means the errors and the deception go inside the number from the address

parts.note: the prime minister's address is 10 Downing Street, and ten is part of it
errors are inaccuracies
to trick is to mislead, so errors that are misleading are errors that trick

explanation.surface: A worried politician sees mistakes distorting a section of a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' suggests a speech, but it means 10 Downing Street, the home of the British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone overwhelmed with fright is terror-stricken, a stronger form of fearful.

clue.text: Somewhat upset about one component of skeleton

indicators.note: about means the reversed phrase goes around the numeral for one
upset in a down answer means the phrase for somewhat is turned upside down

parts.note: somewhat means a bit
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone mildly distressed over a single bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reverses A BIT to TIBA, and 'about' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, one of the bones that make up the human skeleton.

clue.text: In violent row, victim may need to call on it

definitions.text: victim may need to call on it

parts.note: hot can mean fierce or violent, as in a hot temper
a line is a row of things

explanation.surface: During a nasty quarrel, someone being hurt may need to phone for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a line of things in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Helplines for victims of crime or abuse are direct phone services that people call in a crisis.

clue.text: Saw a year in prison cut by precisely 50 per cent

indicators.note: in means a and the year letter go inside the halved prison name
cut by precisely half means only the first half of the prison's name is kept

parts.note: Sing Sing is a famous New York state prison

explanation.surface: A sentence cut neatly in half, with a year served behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see, but it is a noun meaning proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: An old saw is a well-worn proverb or maxim, so a saw is a common saying.

clue.text: In disguise, perhaps, confusing genial bouncers

indicators.note: confusing means the letters of genial bouncers are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Friendly nightclub doormen baffling everyone by going about incognito.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in disguise is meant to be impossible to identify, which is one example of being unrecognisable, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Person in last quarter of life could be this

definitions.text: Person in last quarter of life could be this

parts.words: Person in last quarter of life could be this
parts.note: someone in the final stretch of a long life has usually retired and draws a state allowance

explanation.surface: A musing on what an elderly person is likely to be.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a cryptic description: anyone in the last twenty-odd years of an eighty-year life is probably retired and receiving an old-age allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: An elderly retired person living on a state or company payment is the obvious occupant of life's final quarter.

clue.text: Crazy British lawyer's brief

parts.note: a brief, shortened form of attorney, the American word for lawyer, is atty

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on the short summary a British barrister has prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like a barrister's case papers, but it means a shortened form of the word attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: Batty is informal slang for mad or eccentric, a direct synonym of crazy.

clue.text: Without energy, again experience ease

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for again experience goes around the energy letter

parts.note: to experience something again is to relive it
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A lethargic person seeking to recapture a past feeling of comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but here it carries its old meaning of outside, so RELIVE wraps round E.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease pain or worry is to relieve it, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Start off part of 'Hamlet' with new speech

indicators.note: start off tells us to drop the opening letter of the character's name

parts.note: Horatio is Hamlet's loyal friend, a role in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: An actor opening a scene from Shakespeare's tragedy with a freshly written monologue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like a section of the text, but it is a role in the play: the prince's loyal friend.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal public address, so it is a kind of speech.

clue.text: Small instrument like a scalpel

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
a harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: Describing a tiny surgical tool as resembling a scalpel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests a surgical tool beside the scalpel, but it is the musical kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel's defining quality is its keen cutting edge, so being keen-edged is being like one.

clue.text: Made unclear statement about former pupil's recovery

parts.note: a former pupil of a British school is an old boy, OB, here with the possessive S
a statement about someone's recovery would say that they are cured

explanation.surface: A vague announcement concerning an old pupil getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statement about' frames the rest: the statement on the old boy's recovery is 'OB's cured'. OB, old boy, is British for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to make it hard to see or understand, so the past form means made unclear.

clue.text: Cut in play? Possibly — certainly not in character

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of cut in play may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: An actor wonders whether a line was cut from a play because it didn't fit the role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In character' suggests acting, but it means typical of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour that is out of character for someone is not usual for them, i.e. atypical.

clue.text: Military HQ in which sides' meetings are invariably obtuse

definitions.meaning: the US Department of Defense headquarters in Arlington, Virginia

definitions.text: in which sides' meetings are invariably obtuse
definitions.meaning: a regular five-sided figure has every interior angle at 108 degrees, more than a right angle

explanation.surface: A dig at army top brass, whose meetings are always slow-witted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sides' meetings' looks like conferences between parties, but means corners where the sides of a shape meet; 'obtuse' means wider than ninety degrees, not stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: The American defence headquarters is named for its five-sided shape, whose corners all exceed a right angle.

clue.text: Driver, in turn, gripped by epic scorer

indicators.note: gripped by means the word for turn is held inside the composer's name

parts.note: Richard Wagner composed, or scored, vast epic operas such as the Ring cycle
a turn in a game is a go

explanation.surface: A motorist taking a bend while gripped by a stirring film soundtrack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' suggests sport, but it is a composer who writes scores.
explanation.definitionFit: A waggoner is a person who drives a horse-drawn wagon, so an old kind of driver.

clue.text: Relatively loud speakers — they can be heard in court

definitions.meaning: from the proverb that deeds speak louder than words

definitions.text: they can be heard in court
definitions.meaning: lawsuits brought before a judge are heard in court

explanation.surface: Loudspeakers whose sound carries all the way to the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half rests on the saying that deeds speak louder than words: they are 'relatively loud'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deeds speak louder than words in the proverb, and lawsuits are legal proceedings heard by a court.

clue.text: Head of state moving to centre, in a sense

indicators.note: head of picks out the leading letter of the word state as the piece that shifts
moving to centre says that leading letter travels into the middle of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A political leader shifting towards the middle ground, in some sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Shifting the S of STATE into the middle gives TA-S-TE. 'Moving to centre' reads like a politician's change of stance.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is one of the five senses, alongside sight, hearing, smell and touch.

clue.text: Persuaded to accept current monarch, in private

indicators.note: to accept means the persuaded word with the monarch letters takes the current symbol inside

parts.note: someone sold on an idea has been persuaded of it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone talked into accepting the reigning sovereign, behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adverbial 'in private', but it is the army's lowest rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A private is the lowest-ranking member of an army, an ordinary serving soldier.

clue.text: Did not bid spades after shuffle

indicators.note: after a shuffle the letters of spades come out in a different order

explanation.surface: A bridge player declining to bid in spades once the cards are dealt.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge a player who makes no bid says 'no bid' or 'pass', so having declined they passed.

clue.text: Divine female's cunning is holding me back

indicators.note: holding means the reversed pronoun sits inside the joined word for cunning plus is

parts.note: art can mean craft or cunning, as in artful

indicators.note: back means the pronoun me is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A goddess's guile is keeping the speaker in check.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's after 'female' is only a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis is the Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon, so a female deity.

clue.text: Troublemaker that affects concentration when drinking

definitions.meaning: a person who stirs up trouble between others
tonic or soda added to spirits dilutes the drink

explanation.surface: A rowdy person whose company makes it hard to focus while having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concentration' suggests mental focus, but it means the strength of alcohol in a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrer who causes trouble is called this, and so is a soft drink added to dilute spirits.

clue.text: Second flier showing business plan about island

parts.note: CO, short for company, stands for a business

indicators.note: about means the word for plan goes around the island letter

parts.note: a plot is a scheme or plan

explanation.surface: An airline hopeful pitching a business plan involving an island route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps PLOT round I, giving PILOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The co-pilot is the second-in-command at an aircraft's controls, the other flier in the cockpit.

clue.text: Some Indians take legal action in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means the word for taking legal action is to be heard rather than spelt, and it sounds the same as the answer

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action against someone

explanation.surface: Members of a Native American nation going to court, at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' reads as a court session, fitting the legal surface, but it signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sioux are a group of Native American peoples of the Great Plains, so some American Indians.

clue.text: Getting through, carry a head inside

indicators.note: inside says the word for a head goes within the word for carry

parts.note: to carry something somewhere is to bring it
a head, as in prices per person, means each

explanation.surface: Instructions for getting past an obstacle by hauling something on top of your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A head' means per person, EACH, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaching a wall or defence means breaking a way through it, so getting through.

clue.text: Untidiness is cause of ill feeling

definitions.meaning: a messy, jumbled state, as of a room in chaos
a medical complaint or illness that makes someone feel unwell

explanation.surface: A neat-freak's claim that mess breeds resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill feeling' looks like resentment, but it means physically feeling ill, as from a medical condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a state of mess and a disease or ailment, such as a digestive complaint.

clue.text: Gold put in cast, mostly, for old coin

indicators.note: put in means the gold letters go inside the shortened word for cast
mostly means the word for cast loses its last letter

parts.note: to cast something is to fling it
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Pouring gold into a mould, almost entirely, to make an old coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests metal poured into a mould, matching the gold, but it means throw. A florin was a British two-shilling coin, worth ten pence after 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: The florin is a former British coin, worth two shillings, no longer minted.
